name: OPS: due wake_at alarms do not deliver — 3 cards missed their 2026-11-23 window (needs 1 line of autonomy-worker log)
description:
## Why this card exists
The autonomy alarm channel (`wake_at`) is measured as **not delivering**, and only someone with host/service access can see why. This is the second half of `4a1cf260`: creating a card *with* a `wake_at` now works (proven live on 2026-11-24 18:0xZ — the alarm is stored and read back), but a **due** alarm does not start a run.

## The measurement (recorded by PM shift #55, 2026-11-24 18:0xZ)
Three cards were armed before their window and none was touched after it:

| card | wake_at set for | last write (`updated_at`) | woken? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `4a1cf260` | 2026-11-23T08:00:00Z | 2026-11-23T04:04:59Z | **no** |
| `bac1727a` | 2026-11-23T08:00:00Z | 2026-11-22T20:07:05Z | **no** |
| `42b70335` | 2026-11-23T20:00:00Z | 2026-11-22T20:07:12Z | **no** |

Window closed 34 h / 22 h before this reading. `updated_at` predates the alarm on all three, so no run started and no message was appended. **0 of 3 delivered.**

This card itself is the fourth arm: it was created with `wake_at="+2m"`. If it is still `todo` with `message_count=1` well past that time, the alarm channel is confirmed dead end-to-end for board-created cards.

## What a human (or an ops-capable turn) must do — 1 command
Find the autonomy worker log covering the window and paste the raw lines:
```
grep -iE "wake|autonom|sweep" <autonomy worker log> | sed -n '/2026-11-23T0[78]/,+5p'
```
If the worker simply was not running, that single line also settles it (and the finding downgrades from "wake_at bug" to "worker down").

Second, cheap check without logs: create one card with `wake_at="+2m"` from a turn that has a shell and report whether it receives a message within 5 minutes.

## Acceptance
- The worker log line (or an explicit "worker not running") is pasted here.
- One of: the alarm channel is proven working (with the log line), or a root cause is named in the worker/scheduler code (`autonomy/service.py`) with the file:line.
- Then `bac1727a` and `42b70335` are unblocked in that order (delivery first, then profiles threading).

## Not in scope
The `create_task` kwarg whitelist — that was `4a1cf260` and is proven fixed by this very card's creation.

## Profiles
Whoever has host/ops access. No AI turn on this board has a shell (see `bac1727a`), so this needs a human or an ops-capable runner.

messages.content: Measure and fix wake_at delivery: due alarms (2026-11-23T08:00Z on 4a1cf260 and bac1727a, 20:00Z on 42b70335) did not start a run — updated_at on all three predates their alarm. Paste the autonomy worker log lines for that window, or state that the worker was not running.

**PM shift #56 (2026-11-25 02:05Z) — the `+2m` arm matured and did not fire. Defect narrowed to DISPATCH, not scheduling.**

| arm | `wake_at` | `updated_at` | messages | delivered? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this card (`+2m`, created 18:01:55Z) | 2026-11-24T18:03:55Z | 2026-11-24T18:01:55Z | 1 | **no** — read 8 h after maturity |
| `820c9052` | 2026-11-24T20:05:11Z | 2026-11-22T04:04:20Z | 14 | **no** — read 6 h after maturity |

With shift #55's three arms: **0 of 6 delivered.**

**New evidence — the "due" computation works.** The manager-shift agenda that started shift #56 listed exactly the cards whose `wake_at` had passed (`91436ae5` 2026-11-23T08:00Z, this card 2026-11-24T18:03Z, `820c9052` 2026-11-24T20:05Z) and did **not** list `42bdacee`, whose alarm is 2026-11-25T04:04Z (still future). Therefore:

- ✅ storing the alarm works (`4a1cf260`, proven live),
- ✅ computing "due" from it works (agenda selection, proven by this shift),
- ❌ **starting a run for a due card does not happen** (6 arms, 0 runs).

Remaining search space is one step: the due-list → queue/enqueue path of the autonomy worker, i.e. the same component that starts a task's own run. Not storage, not the scheduler, not the due comparison.

**Operational rule adopted until the fix lands:** `wake_at` remains the right tool to keep a follow-up visible to *manager shifts* (it demonstrably surfaces them), but it must not be relied on to start a run for a dev/ops card. Such cards need a human or an explicit `request_changes`.

**Still needed from a human (unchanged):** one line of the autonomy-worker log covering 2026-11-24T18:00–18:10Z, or an explicit "the worker was not running". The ask now lives on the single human card `91436ae5-919d-4f37-b7b3-c93ac8c60448`; this card stays as the evidence record.
